subject: tool:composed-census-t15-operand-provenance
value:
THE PREMISE OF THE CORRECTED PROMOTION ORDERING WAS MEASURED AND IS REFUTED FOR THIS TIER. The run-46 promotion order's item (1), following claim.law.PP_the-smallest-webfrank-rules-are-the-worst-promotion-candidates.20260903.v1, directed a lane to run t15_operand_provenance image-wide and work every rule whose function shows an operand-VALUE difference as a PointLineDist2D-class candidate - real source bugs hiding under a recolor verdict. Run at commit c621fcbac on a green build (`ninja -j2` printing `build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK`), `python tools/gdl/composed_census/t15_operand_provenance.py --pinned --out build/GUNE5D/pr_provenance.json` screened 290 paired functions with a differing body: NOT-REGISTER-ONLY 176, PROVENANCE-CONSISTENT 76, ERROR 18, BASE-FORM-DIFF 7, UNDECIDED 6, EXCHANGE 4, OPERAND-VALUE-DIFF 3. NOT ONE of the three OPERAND-VALUE-DIFF rows is a source bug.

THE THREE, individually. (1) game/movie/movieplayer::fn_800DBE98 and (2) game/ps2/fakelib::sceRead are excluded by the screen's own staging rule - both declare `instruction_permutation` pre-recolor stages, so our raw object is not the image their rule recolors, and the screen prints them under a STAGED BASE banner rather than as findings. (3) game/sys/memcard::drawMemCardMessage at +0x1ec, +0x1fc and +0x20c is the one open finding attempt.T15_tool-queue-15-nine-items-one-refuted-mandate-and-a-provenance-backlog.20260903.v1 left for a next lane, and it is CLOSED HERE as a systematic false positive of the screen's weakest evidence class.

THE drawMemCardMessage CLOSURE. The T15 record asked the right question - 'the next lane should decide whether that path can reach +0x1ec at all' - and the answer is YES, it can, so the phis do NOT collapse: at +0x1bc retail tests `cmplwi r26,0` and at +0x1c4 branches `beq ->1ec`, where r26 is the MBNewBlit result, initialised to zero at +0x24 `li r26,0` and assigned only on the strcmp-equal path. When MBNewBlit returns NULL the blit path falls into +0x1ec and reads the register that only the MBNewTempQuad path defines. But the reachability was never the deciding fact. Both phis have the SAME first component - `('call', 50, 'g', 3)`, the shared MBNewTempQuad return - and differ only in the second, target `('entry','g',25)` against ours `('entry','g',28)`. Those are the ENTRY VALUES of a callee-saved register that the function saves at +0xc `stmw r20,136(r1)` and restores at +0x244 `lmw`, and under ANY renaming sigma with sigma(r25)=r28 the entry token maps entry(r25) to entry(r28) - so the screen, which compares entry tokens as raw architectural-register identities rather than under the running renaming, reports a difference for every such phi it ever meets, no matter what the function does. The finding is a fact about the screen, not about drawMemCardMessage. AGENTS.md discipline 14 in its exact form: a guard's refusal is a measurement of the guard. Two consequences worth acting on: the screen's entry token should be renaming-relative, and separately, the retail function does contain a latent uninitialised read on the MBNewBlit-returns-NULL path which OUR SOURCE REPRODUCES FAITHFULLY at 204/204 instructions - it must not be 'fixed'.

THE FOUR NON-STAGED LEADS FROM THE WG COMPLEMENT, screened on integrator relay. The WG lane's wg_identical_slot_provenance.py covers this screen's blind spot (slots where the two words are identical but read different values) and fired 15 of 152, of which 11 declare pre-recolor stages, leaving four unscreened non-staged leads. All four were read from the aligned RAW view and ALL FOUR ARE VALUE-EQUAL: game/game/player::load_player_model +0x2c, target `add r7,r29,r30` against ours `add r7,r27,r30` - the r30 slot is identical and reads potionicon_tab base on one side and index*76 on the other, but `add` is commutative and both sides compute base+index*76, a COMMUTED pair; game/anim/anim::InitAnim +0xb4, target `fmul f0,f1,f0` against ours `fmul f0,f3,f0` - looks like PointLineDist2D but tracing back shows target forms (K*n) then (K*n)*S and ours forms (n*K) then S*(n*K), the same GROUPING with commuted operands, hence bit-identical (see attempt.PR_initanim-the-inner-multiply-follows-source-order-and-the-outer-is-canonicalised.20260903.v1); game/mb/mb_blit::DrawBlit +0x220-+0x22c, four `fmuls` sharing a common factor that retail carries in the rC slot and we carry in rA, a commuted pair four times over; game/game/player::PlayerProcessPowerups +0xe68, `fcmpu cr0,f1,f0` - the WORD IS IDENTICAL in both streams while +0xe64 loads the compared field into f1 in retail and f0 in ours, so the two operands are exchanged, and the branch at +0xe6c is `beq`, for which fcmpu is symmetric in both the ordered and the unordered result. That last one is worth stating as its own discriminator, because PointLineDist2D's second defect WAS a reversed fcmpu: a reversed floating-point compare is a correctness question only when the consuming branch is ORDERED (blt/bgt/ble/bge) or when NaN handling is observable; on beq/bne it is exactly neutral.

SO: across 290 screened functions, 152 rule-served pairs, three OPERAND-VALUE-DIFF rows and four independent identical-slot leads, the PointLineDist2D class has a measured population of ONE, and that one was already found and fixed. The corrected ordering's item (1) is a REFUTED PREMISE and, per AGENTS.md discipline 5, that is the deliverable. A future run should not re-run this screen as a bug hunt; it should run it as a PRE-SCREEN before granting any new unproven_recolor_audit escape, which is what the tool's own docstring says it is for.
